overview.text: The testes (singular = testis) are the male gonads—that is, the male reproductive organs.
overview.label: 27.1 Testes

overview.text: They produce both sperm and androgens, such as testosterone, and are active throughout the reproductive lifespan.
overview.label: 27.1 Testes

overview.text: The bulk of semen is produced by three critical accessory glands of the male reproductive system: the seminal vesicles, the prostate, and the bulbourethral glands.
overview.label: 27.1 Duct System

testes.text: The testes (singular = testis) are the male gonads—that is, the male reproductive organs.
testes.label: 27.1 Testes

testes.text: Beneath the tunica vaginalis is the tunica albuginea, a tough, white, dense connective tissue layer covering the testis itself.
testes.label: 27.1 Testes

testes.text: Not only does the tunica albuginea cover the outside of the testis, it also invaginates to form septa that divide the testis into 300 to 400 structures called lobules.
testes.label: 27.1 Testes

testes.text: Within the lobules, sperm develop in structures called seminiferous tubules.
testes.label: 27.1 Testes

testes.text: During the seventh month of the developmental period of a male fetus, each testis moves through the abdominal musculature to descend into the scrotal cavity.
testes.label: 27.1 Testes

epididymis.text: Though the epididymis does not take up much room in its tightly coiled state, it would be approximately 6 m (20 feet) long if straightened.
epididymis.label: 27.1 Role of the Epididymis

epididymis.text: Sperm enter the head of the epididymis and are moved along predominantly by the contraction of smooth muscles lining the epididymal tubes.
epididymis.label: 27.1 Role of the Epididymis

epididymis.text: The more mature sperm are then stored in the tail of the epididymis (the final section) until ejaculation occurs.
epididymis.label: 27.1 Role of the Epididymis

deferent.text: During ejaculation, sperm exit the tail of the epididymis and are pushed by smooth muscle contraction to the ductus deferens (also called the vas deferens).
deferent.label: 27.1 Duct System

deferent.text: From each epididymis, each ductus deferens extends superiorly into the abdominal cavity through the inguinal canal in the abdominal wall.
deferent.label: 27.1 Duct System

deferent.text: From here, the ductus deferens continues posteriorly to the pelvic cavity, ending posterior to the bladder where it dilates in a region called the ampulla (meaning “flask”).
deferent.label: 27.1 Duct System

seminal.text: The paired seminal vesicles are glands that contribute approximately 60 percent of the semen volume.
seminal.label: 27.1 Seminal Vesicles

seminal.text: Seminal vesicle fluid contains large amounts of fructose, which is used by the sperm mitochondria to generate ATP to allow movement through the female reproductive tract.
seminal.label: 27.1 Seminal Vesicles

seminal.text: The fluid, now containing both sperm and seminal vesicle secretions, next moves into the associated ejaculatory duct, a short structure formed from the ampulla of the ductus deferens and the duct of the seminal vesicle.
seminal.label: 27.1 Seminal Vesicles

prostate.text: About the size of a walnut, the prostate is formed of both muscular and glandular tissues.
prostate.label: 27.1 Prostate Gland

prostate.text: It excretes an alkaline, milky fluid to the passing seminal fluid—now called semen—that is critical to first coagulate and then decoagulate the semen following ejaculation.
prostate.label: 27.1 Prostate Gland

prostate.text: The prostatic urethra passes through the prostate gland.
prostate.label: 25.2 Male Urethra

penis.text: The penis is the male organ of copulation (sexual intercourse).
penis.label: 27.1 The Penis

penis.text: The shaft is composed of three column-like chambers of erectile tissue that span the length of the shaft.
penis.label: 27.1 The Penis

penis.text: Each of the two larger lateral chambers is called a corpus cavernosum (plural = corpora cavernosa).
penis.label: 27.1 The Penis

penis.text: Together, these make up the bulk of the penis.
penis.label: 27.1 The Penis

spongiosum.text: The corpus spongiosum, which can be felt as a raised ridge on the erect penis, is a smaller chamber that surrounds the spongy, or penile, urethra.
spongiosum.label: 27.1 The Penis

spongiosum.text: The shaft is composed of three column-like chambers of erectile tissue that span the length of the shaft.
spongiosum.label: 27.1 The Penis

glans.text: The skin from the shaft extends down over the glans and forms a collar called the prepuce (or foreskin).
glans.label: 27.1 The Penis

glans.text: The foreskin also contains a dense concentration of nerve endings, and both lubricate and protect the sensitive skin of the glans penis.
glans.label: 27.1 The Penis

urethra.text: The length of the male urethra varies between people but averages 20 cm in length.
urethra.label: 25.2 Male Urethra

urethra.text: It is divided into four regions: the preprostatic urethra, the prostatic urethra, the membranous urethra, and the spongy or penile urethra.
urethra.label: 25.2 Male Urethra

urethra.text: The prostatic urethra passes through the prostate gland.
urethra.label: 25.2 Male Urethra

penile-vessels.text: Penile erections are the result of vasocongestion, or engorgement of the tissues because of more arterial blood flowing into the penis than is leaving in the veins.
penile-vessels.label: 27.1 The Penis

penile-vessels.text: Release of NO activates a signaling pathway that results in relaxation of the smooth muscles that surround the penile arteries, causing them to dilate.
penile-vessels.label: 27.1 The Penis

bladder.text: In males, the anatomy is similar, minus the uterus, and with the addition of the prostate inferior to the bladder.
bladder.label: 25.2 Bladder

bladder.text: The bladder is a retroperitoneal organ whose "dome" distends superiorly when the bladder is filling with urine.
bladder.label: 25.2 Bladder

gaps: The dataset has no meshes for the scrotum, the spermatic cord, the ejaculatory ducts, the bulbourethral glands or the prepuce.
The urethra is one mesh in the dataset; its four regions are not shown separately.
BodyParts3D is one male body. It has no female organs, so there is no female reproductive workstation yet.
notes: OpenStax's current edition calls this the testicular reproductive system (section 27.1).
The ejaculatory ducts are named in the tour text but are not in the 3D model.
Size: each testis in this model is 2.9 cm along its longest axis (build/measure.py). OpenStax 27.1 gives about 4 to 5 cm for an adult testis.
